plan.reason: V4 has the highest risk score and concerns a stateful, single-replica checkout dependency. A pod kill directly tests restart behavior and whether persistent cart state remains usable.

prediction.summary: Cart reads and writes may fail during restart, causing checkout errors; persistent storage should prevent silent cart loss after recovery.

plan.reason: Paymentservice is a single replica on the revenue-generating checkout path. A service outage directly tests whether checkout fails closed and whether frontend traffic receives an appropriate response.

prediction.summary: Payment and checkout requests should fail or become substantially slower while paymentservice is unavailable; browsing may remain available.

plan.reason: The frontend is the single entrypoint and has one replica. Killing it tests whether the site becomes unreachable during recreation, using customer-facing error and latency criteria rather than target health.

prediction.summary: Requests reaching the site should fail or experience severe latency during frontend restart, temporarily affecting all user-facing flows.

plan.reason: The checkout orchestrator is a single-replica critical path service. A substantial delay tests latency propagation and timeout handling without repeating only pod-availability failures.

prediction.summary: Checkout requests should experience sharply increased latency and may time out, while non-checkout frontend functionality may remain available.

replan_note: No prior experiments have been run, so rankings are based on severity, risk score, checkout-path impact, and statefulness. V2 then tests total site availability, and V3 broadens coverage to latency and timeout propagation using a different fault type. Results should re-rank remaining hypotheses based on observed customer error, latency, and integrity impact.
